precedence: The binding contract (the plan's Must NOT have list, AGENTS.md and the workspace lint tables) outranks the inherited recommendations quoted from violations.md. Where an inherited recommendation is stricter or more specific than the contract (zerocopy layouts, an as_conversions deny, compile-time schema checks), the row says so and it stays a review prompt, never a gate.

rules.check: Reviewer searches the diff for a literal or logic block repeated across files; each must become one named constant or helper.
Ids, incarnations, generations, tokens and offsets are distinct newtypes on every new boundary; no bare String or u64 crosses a public API.
Functions stay under 100 lines and the cognitive-complexity threshold; reviewer confirms dispatch, validation, I/O and persistence are separate functions.
No `as` cast to a numeric type anywhere in the roots; conversions use From or try_from with an explicit overflow policy.
Each boundary error is a thiserror enum with kind() and hint(); no String kinds, no Box<dyn Error> at a public boundary.
At most three parameters per signature, receiver included; no boolean mode flags (pedantic fn_params_excessive_bools).
Every .rs file under the roots stays at or below 250 pure lines of code; an oversized file is split along a responsibility seam.
Closed sets are enums from the wire to storage; reviewer rejects string-typed states or kinds.

No `let _ =` over a call, await, `?` or macro and no `.ok();` statement discard; failures propagate or are reported, never turned into Null or success. The few accepted `.ok();` discards are listed below with their reason, and an exemption that no longer matches fails source-check.
Spawn, exit, I/O and protocol failures stay distinct variants; reviewer rejects one catch-all message for several causes.
Every unsafe block carries a SAFETY comment, one operation, and sits behind a safe wrapper with native or Miri evidence.
Boundary input is parsed once into a typed value with deny_unknown_fields; nothing re-validates a parsed value.
No glob imports (pedantic wildcard_imports) and no shared mutable out-parameters.
Matches over owned enums name every variant; unknown frames are rejected with a typed error, never dropped.
Same 250 pure-LOC limit; wire types and CLI definitions live in separate modules.
Tests are hermetic and every assertion can fail: no assert!(true), no comparison of an expression with itself, no ambient environment.
Library diagnostics go through tracing with structured fields; println!/eprintln!/dbg! are lint errors outside tests.
Every acquired resource has an RAII guard; one failed accept or child never takes down its parent loop.
Comments state a constraint or a reason; reviewer deletes stale, orphaned or restating comments.
Waits subscribe to a readiness signal before triggering; no fixed-interval polling, no fixed sleeps in tests, buffers are reused.
Dead code fails the clippy -D warnings step of scripts/check.sh; it is deleted, never primed or silenced.
Arithmetic on untrusted or counter values states its overflow policy with checked, wrapping or saturating operations.
A poisoned lock becomes a typed error that is handled; reviewer rejects silent into_inner().
No #[allow] or cfg_attr(..., allow(...)); a lint is silenced only with #[expect(lint, reason = ...)] on one item.
No pass-through wrappers or near-identical names; layers are named by role.
No unwrap/expect outside tests (clippy.toml allows them only in tests).
Every codec, parser and public async entry point ships with tests that fail on the regression they name.
Every spawned task and loop takes a cancellation token and is joined on shutdown.
Each atomic uses the weakest correct ordering with a comment stating why.
Resolved values are built, not written back into inputs or parameters.
Names follow the Rust API guidelines; self-less helpers are free functions.
Framing and binary parsing live in the protocol wire module. The inherited zerocopy-layout recommendation is not part of the binding contract and stays guidance.
A vetted library replaces a hand-rolled parser or constant shim whenever one is already in the dependency graph.
Flags and predicates have positive names.
Blocking SQLite and PTY work runs in spawn_blocking or a dedicated thread, never on a Tokio worker.
Every queue, mailbox and retention window has an advertised bound with backpressure; no per-frame large allocation.
An error is logged once, at the boundary that handles it; helpers return errors.
One tracing pipeline; no hard-coded log files or second logging stack.
No defensive fallback on a value the code just proved.
No panic!, todo!, unimplemented! or unreachable! outside tests.
Every flag and subcommand is declared through clap derive; argv is never pre-parsed by hand.
Lifecycle states are types or closed enums, not runtime boolean flags.
A failure that disables a feature logs at warn or above.
Same rule as PROG-IRON-unwrap.
Paths stay PathBuf/OsStr end to end; display() appears only in human-readable output.
Same rule as PROG-IRON-cast.
Matches over std or owned enums name every variant; a wildcard arm is used only for a foreign #[non_exhaustive] enum.
A pass claim must be backed by parsed exit statuses, recomputed assertions and a binary hash; evidence-audit rejects prose PASS banners and forged assertions.
Waits start from a caller-supplied cursor; subscriptions are acknowledged and heartbeated.
Reads and status never start a daemon; restore and risky writes are explicit.
Every failure is a structured {kind, message, hint} with a stable kind.
deny.toml exists at the workspace root and cargo-deny runs in CI.

The workspace lint tables deny unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, let_underscore_must_use and allow_attributes with pedantic and nursery enabled, and every member inherits them. The inherited as_conversions deny is covered by the numeric-cast rule instead.
Protocol semantics are the same on every OS and the schema is generated from the Rust types. The inherited 'checked at compile time, not parsed as JSON' wording is guidance.
One multiplexed connection with correlated ids; sends return admission without waiting for status.
Unknown targeting fields are rejected with a field path; no call falls back to a focused pane (EXCL-006).
No std Mutex guard is held across an await (clippy await_holding_lock is in the denied all group).
rust-toolchain.toml pins the channel.
Every parser has a named error type; no String errors.
Same rule as PROG-SMELL-2.
The runtime has no screen heuristics to rank against a report: they are excluded outright (EXCL-008, EXCL-009). Declared status authority is IDEAL-066, proven by scenario agent/status.
Every event uses the one EventEnvelope generated into the OpenRPC schema.
History is a bounded API read with truncation fields, not a screen snapshot.
Same rule as SLOP-8: block on readiness, never sleep-retry.

exclusions.check: A misspelled target field or flag is a typed error before dispatch, never data about a focused pane: quality/gates asserts `ovis-terminal --json schema openrpc --target focused` exits 2 with kind usage on stderr and nothing on stdout.

Every managed invocation keeps an identity, bounded output and an exit outcome: each gate run is recorded with its argv, exit status and full JSON report, and plugin runs keep bounded output and exit results (todo 46).
Failure state stays queryable instead of expiring as a banner: every gate verdict is a JSON report appended to the evidence file, and evidence-audit rejects a printed PASS banner as evidence.

dropped_result_exemptions.reason: A tokio oneshot reply fails only when the requester has dropped its receiver (it cancelled or timed out); the scheduler has nobody to tell, and the work's own effects are already recorded where the requester can query them.
